property_summary: The sum of `Put`s minus the sum of successful `Collect`s for an account must equal the recorded balance; the bug overwrites balance on the second `Put`, making `acc.balance` less than the difference.
After two consecutive Put calls by the same sender, the contract balance should equal the sum of the two sent amounts, but the bug overwrites the balance instead of accumulating it.

After any number of Put calls by any sender, the sum of all msg.value sent by that sender must equal the cumulative deposited balance for that sender as recorded in Acc[sender].balance. The bug overwrites the balance on each Put, making the recorded balance equal only to the last msg.value instead of the total.

For any two Put calls with msg.value v1 then v2 by the same sender where unlockTime increases, Acc[sender].balance must eventually equal v1+v2; the bug overwrites balance to v2, so only v2 is retained.

After any sequence of Put calls by the same sender, the contract's total balance equals the sum of all msg.value sent by that sender; the bug overwrites balance on each Put, so the contract holds less than the total sent.

After any Put call, the contract's total balance (address(c).balance) must equal the sum of all holder balances recorded in Acc; the mutant breaks this invariant because it increments the holder's balance by _unlockTime instead of msg.value.

After a caller calls Put with some unlock time and msg.value, their Acc balance can never increase by more than msg.value; the bug lets it increase by _unlockTime, violating this invariant for some inputs.

After any call to Put, the recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance plus the original msg.value must remain at least as large as the new Acc[msg.sender].balance; the mutant breaks this by setting balance to the prior balance plus _unlockTime, which can be less than msg.value.

After Put, the recorded Acc balance of the caller must be strictly greater than before by at least msg.value minus any potential overflow; the mutant increases it by _unlockTime instead of msg.value, so the balance increase can be less than msg.value when _unlockTime < msg.value.

After any call to Put, the contract's ETH balance must increase by exactly the msg.value sent; the mutant breaks this because it adds _unlockTime to the caller's Acc balance without accounting for the actual msg.value, causing the ETH balance increase to mismatch the msg.value.

For any msg.sender and msg.value, after Put, acc.balance must be msg.value plus the previous balance, which holds when overflow is guarded; the mutant removes the overflow check and allows balance to wrap around via huge msg.value, breaking the invariant.

For any sender and any sequence of calls, the sum of all Put/fallback msg.values must never overflow the sender's recorded balance; the mutant removes the overflow guard, allowing acc.balance to wrap around for huge msg.value inputs.

For any address A and any msg.value V sent via Put or the fallback, the sum of the previous Acc[A].balance plus V must be >= the previous Acc[A].balance (no overflow); the bug removes this check, allowing the balance to overflow.

For any address and any call sequence, the sum of the previous recorded balance plus the msg.value of the next Put must never be less than the previous balance (no overflow); the bug omits this overflow check, allowing the balance to wrap around.

For any sender and any msg.value sent via Put, if the previous balance is non-zero, the new balance must be strictly greater than the previous balance; the mutant removes the overflow check, allowing a huge msg.value to cause wrap-around making the new balance smaller.

After any call to Put, the caller's balance stored in Acc must be at least the sent msg.value minus any previous balance, but the bug subtracts msg.value instead of adding it, so the balance becomes unexpectedly lower.

After a call to Put, the caller's balance stored in Acc must be strictly greater than its previous balance by at least msg.value, but the bug subtracts msg.value instead of adding it, so the new balance becomes smaller instead of larger.

After calling Put with a positive value, the contract's ether balance must increase by at least msg.value, reflecting that deposited funds are added, but the bug subtracts msg.value from the user's balance instead, causing the contract's balance to not increase as expected.

For any caller and any positive deposit, the caller's Acc balance after Put is strictly greater than before Put (by msg.value). The bug subtracts instead of adds, so the balance decreases or becomes zero/underflowed.

After any call to Put, the sum of all balances in the Acc mapping must equal the contract's Ether balance; the bug subtracts msg.value from the caller's balance instead of adding it, breaking this invariant.

For any user with balance exactly equal to withdrawal amount and satisfying other conditions, the reference allows full withdrawal leaving zero balance, while the mutant with strict inequality rejects it, breaking the invariant that a user can withdraw their entire balance.

For any admissible call to Collect, if the sender's balance is at least MinSum and the unlockTime has passed, then a withdrawal of exactly the full balance succeeds on the reference but fails on the buggy contract that requires strict greater-than, violating the invariant that a Collect of the full balance never reverts.

For any user with balance >= MinSum and after unlockTime, a withdrawal of any amount <= balance always succeeds on the reference, but the mutant may revert when amount == balance due to the strict inequality.

For any user with balance >= MinSum and after unlockTime, a withdrawal of an amount equal to the balance always succeeds on the reference, but the strict inequality in the mutant causes it to revert when amount equals balance, breaking the invariant that Collect never reverts for a full balance withdrawal.

For any user with a balance of at least MinSum and after unlockTime, a withdrawal of an amount exactly equal to the balance succeeds (reduces balance to 0) on the reference, but the buggy contract rejects it because it requires acc.balance > _am.
In Collect, when acc.balance equals exactly the requested amount (acc.balance == _am), the reference completes the withdrawal while the mutant reverts due to the _am+1 check.

For any sender, after a successful Collect of amount X, the sender's balance in C decreases by exactly X; the mutant reverts when the sender tries to withdraw the full balance, leaving the balance unchanged.

For any account that has a positive balance recorded in the contract and a past unlock time, a Collect call for the exact recorded balance succeeds (reducing the balance to 0) in the reference, but the mutant reverts because it requires the recorded balance to be strictly greater than the requested amount.

For any sender with sufficient balance and unlocked funds, a Collect of an amount strictly less than the balance succeeds in the reference, but in the mutant a Collect of balance-1 reverts because the check requires balance >= amount+1, which fails when amount = balance-1.

For any sender with a positive balance and unlocked funds, a Collect call for 1 wei less than the full balance succeeds in the reference but reverts in the mutant because the mutant requires balance >= amount+1, which fails when amount = balance-1.
After a successful Collect call, the sender's balance should be reduced by the withdrawn amount; the buggy version lacks the balance update, so the balance remains unchanged allowing double-spending.

After a Collect or revert, the sender's recorded balance in Acc must equal the initial balance minus the transferred amount if the call succeeded, or remain unchanged if it reverted; the mutant omits the balance decrement on success, so a succeeding Collect leaves the balance unchanged.
After a successful Collect, the sender's Acc balance must decrease by exactly the withdrawn amount; the mutant omits the balance update, so balance stays unchanged allowing re-entrant double-spend.

After any successful Collect, the caller's recorded Acc balance must decrease by at least the withdrawn amount; the buggy version omits the balance decrement, so a successful Collect leaves the balance unchanged, violating this invariant.
After a successful Collect, the caller's Acc balance must be strictly less than before the call; the buggy version omits the balance decrement, so balance stays unchanged.

After any call to Collect, the caller's balance must strictly exceed the unlock time to proceed, which is enforced by > in the original but violated by >= in the mutant, allowing a withdrawal exactly at unlockTime.

In the correct contract, a Collect call exactly at unlockTime with sufficient balance and MinSum reverts (or leaves the balance unchanged), whereas the mutant allows it to succeed and reduce the balance.
After a Collect call exactly at unlockTime, the caller's Acc balance must remain unchanged in the correct contract, but decreases in the mutant.

The invariant is that after any Collect call, the caller's Acc balance can only decrease if the call was executed strictly after the unlock time; the mutant allows a decrease exactly at the unlock time.
After any Collect call, the caller's balance decreases only if block.timestamp is strictly greater than unlockTime; the mutant allows a decrease also when block.timestamp equals unlockTime.

The rule is that any successfully collected amount is exactly deducted from the caller's balance, and this holds for all inputs in the reference but the bug can prevent collection of exactly MinSum balance even when conditions are otherwise met.

For any caller with balance >= MinSum and _am == MinSum and block.timestamp > unlockTime, a Collect call must succeed and reduce balance exactly by _am; the mutant rejects this because it uses > instead of >= for the MinSum check, causing a revert when balance == MinSum.

For any caller with at least MinSum balance and an unlock time in the past, a Collect of any amount up to their balance that meets the MinSum check must succeed; the mutant fails when balance equals MinSum because it requires strictly greater.

For any caller with balance >= _am and _am >= MinSum and block.timestamp > unlockTime, a Collect call that does not revert must reduce balance by exactly _am; the mutant reverts when balance == MinSum because it uses > instead of >=.

For any caller with a balance exactly equal to MinSum, after a Collect of MinSum at a time after unlockTime, their balance should become zero; the mutant reverts because it uses '>' instead of '>=' for the MinSum check.
